title: sdks: unify auth/retries + streaming ergonomics across python/ts/go; parity fixes and v1.55.0 version bumps
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: - Unify authentication and retry behavior across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs; consistent env var, credential helper, and token refresh behavior. - Improve streaming API ergonomics: single unified iterator/async iterator contract and clearer error propagation on partial frames. - Parity fixes for edgecases in Go/TS SDKs (stream close semantics, backpressure in Node). - Bumped SDK versions to v1.55.0 across languages and updated changelogs.
description: This PR unifies auth/retries and streaming ergonomics across the three official SDKs (python/typescript/go) and includes parity fixes and version bumps to v1.55.0. Motivation: inconsistent behavior between SDKs has caused customer confusion and production regressions when switching languages; differences in streaming iterators and retry boundaries led to subtle bugs in long-running streaming sessions. What changed: consolidated auth flow so all SDKs support: 1) credential chain (env > shared cred > metadata), 2) automatic token refresh for short-lived keys, and 3) a unified retry policy with idempotency-aware defaults. Streaming: introduced a single ergonomic surface for streaming responses (sync iterator for Python, async iterator for TS, channel-based reader for Go) with deterministic closure semantics and clearer errors on partial/early termination. Parity fixes: aligned behavior on backpressure (TS), connection reuse (Go), and header propagation (Python). Version bumps: updated package versions and changelogs to v1.55.0 and included migration notes. Checklist: - [x] Specs and tests added/updated for all three SDKs - [x] End-to-end smoke tests against the hosted API - [x] CI green on all language matrices - [x] Changelog entries and release notes - [x] Docs examples updated for new streaming API Backwards compatibility: default retry behavior remains conservative and opt-in changes are gated behind feature flags where necessary. If consumers rely on SDK internals, see migration notes in the changelog. Related: ENG-4832, PM-219.

notes_for_release_engineer: Coordinate staggered rollout for dedicated customers who pin older SDKs. Announce deprecation timeline for legacy streaming helpers in docs. Watch for increased token refresh traffic for short-lived tokens during first 48h after release.
migration_notes: - Python: StreamingIterator is a drop-in replacement for legacy StreamReader; if you used low-level frames, update to new API. - TypeScript: migrations for async iterator (for..await) are straightforward; see examples. - Go: use StreamReader.Close() semantics carefully; Close now signals EOF semantics to server. - Retry policy defaults changed to be idempotency-aware; if you relied on prior behavior, set RETRY_LEGACY=true.
